description: Four-voice pitch shifter: it takes one audio input and shifts it to four pitches set by the volt-per-octave jacks, shaping each voice with an envelope and a filter

params.text: One of the two knobs a screen parameter can be assigned to; with nothing assigned to it, turning it changes nothing
Turn it to move between the parameters on the current page and click it to select one, then turn it to change the value and click again; double-click it to hand a parameter to a CV jack or knob
Opens the page for the audio mode in use; press it again and the list of audio modes appears, which the encoder then steps through
Opens the function page last used; press it again and the list of function pages appears, covering the gates, the envelope, the filter, the vocoder, the audio settings and the system settings

inputs.text: One of the four jacks a screen parameter can be assigned to, 0 to 5V covering the whole of that parameter's range; with nothing assigned to it the jack is read but changes nothing
The audio the module pitch shifts, and the one to use for a single source: it feeds the second audio input as well whenever nothing is patched there
A second audio source, so that two of the four voices can be driven by a different sound; with nothing patched here it reads the first audio input
A gate or trigger for the voice in that colour, read as high above 1V; what it does — fire one envelope, fire several, start a strum or sample the pitches — is set on the Gates page
Sets the pitch of the voice in that colour at 1V per octave, and the module reads it between -4V and +4V, so the shift stops four octaves either way rather than the five the maker's manual gives

outputs.text: One of the two audio outputs, carrying two of the four voices; the Down Mix option on the Audio Settings page sends all four to both outputs instead

notes: almost nothing on this module is set from the panel: the encoder moves the focus between parameters and selects them, and the Mode and Func buttons open the pages carrying them
the four CV jacks and the two knobs do nothing until a screen parameter is assigned to one; focus the parameter, double-click the encoder, and pick the input from the page that pops up
while the pointer is over the encoder, or over a flashing Mode or Func button, the mouse scroll wheel turns the encoder rather than scrolling the rack
the module collects 256 samples before processing them, so there is a delay of at least that between what goes in and what comes out
the note names on the display are only right once the tuner has run; without it they are relative to a C root
three things the maker's manual describes are not in this plugin: there is no MIDI mode, the Calibration page is greyed out, and the display dimming setting has no effect
menu: Capture mouse scroll — turns off the module taking the mouse scroll wheel over the encoder and the buttons, so the wheel scrolls the rack as it normally does
